newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish biker gang war torpedoes Rushdie visit.
newsitem.headline: Danish biker gang war torpedoes Rushdie visit.

text.p: Denmark on Thursday barred author Salman Rushdie from coming to collect an EU literary prize, citing security concerns because of advance publicity and police being too stretched by a Nordic biker gang war.
"The visit this time is known about in advance and we use so many resources to keep an eye on the bikers," Copenhagen police chief Hanne Bech Hansen said.

Rushdie has lived in hiding and with permanent protection since 1989, when Iranian revolutionary leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a death threat, or "fatwa", against him for his novel "The Satanic Verses".
The British writer told Denmark's TV2 television station that the Danish government's explanation was unacceptable.

"This is an exceptional example of political cowardice," the Indian-born writer said. A local Rushdie support committee said he had rejected a government proposal to accept the 20,000 Ecu Aristeion Prize at another opportunity.

Presentation of awards to Rushdie, Austrian writer Christoph Ransmayer and Danish author and translator Thorkild Bjoernvig were to have been made on November 14 in Copenhagen as it is this year's European Cultural Capital, a title which rotates around the EU.
